overall_summary: Analysis of 47 deduplicated Shorts reveals that visceral first-person immersive 'What If You Fell Into...' scenarios and extreme cosmic horror/astronomy physics outperform abstract psychology and repetitive trivia by 5x-10x. The top performers consistently exceed 800-1,000+ views with high like engagement (up to 3.7% like-to-view ratio), particularly videos with runtimes between 19 and 21 seconds. In contrast, repetitive uploads of psychology factoids ('fake memories', 'songs stuck in head') and regurgitated trivia ('octopuses have 3 hearts') suffer severe algorithmic throttling (<50 views).

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Extreme Survival / 'What If You Fell Into...' Hypotheticals
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes), 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes), and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (823 views, 15 likes) dominate both total views and velocity.
winning_patterns.action: Standardize the second-person ('You') experiential hazard format with sensory, body-horror-adjacent astrophysical consequences.

winning_patterns.pattern: Bizarre Planetary Physics & Paradoxical Extremes (19-21s Runtime)
winning_patterns.evidence: Recent release 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' hit 981 views with 21 likes, while 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' reached 1,029 views and 36 likes. Videos running 19-21s capture far more likes and comments than 12-16s clips.
winning_patterns.action: Maintain optimal pacing at 19-21 seconds, front-loading the impossible physical paradox within the first 1.5 seconds.

weak_patterns.evidence: Duplicate uploads of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' flatlined at 5, 10, and 53 views. 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' produced only 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Cease soft psychology tips and eliminate duplicate/near-duplicate re-uploads entirely to protect channel authority.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos titled 'The Eyeball Planet That Could Harbor Life!' (40 views) and 'The Star Colder Than Ice' (83 views) lacked visceral stakes and underperformed active what-if variants.
weak_patterns.action: Convert static descriptive hooks into active physical scenarios that threaten or challenge the viewer.

next_video.concept: What happens to the human body when falling toward a Magnetar (the universe's strongest magnetic monster).
next_video.opening_direction: Instant visual of a dead star distorting starlight, opening voiceover: 'If you fell toward a magnetar, you would die long before ever touching its surface.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that at 1,000 kilometers away, its magnetic field is so violently intense it strips the electrons from your body's atoms, turning you into a cloud of atomic mist.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven 'What If / Falling Into' visceral mechanic that drives FACTVERSE's top-tier views, while pivoting to a completely fresh cosmic terror entity (Magnetars) not yet featured in channel history.
fresh_topic_constraints: Do not reuse exoplanet weather tropes (diamond rain, molten iron, ruby rain, glass sideways).
Do not cover TrES-2b, Gliese 436b, Venus day/year, or J1407b rings.
Ensure factual scientific accuracy regarding magnetic atomic distortion.

experiment: Test whether framing an astrophysical object through an extreme human biological consequence ('magnetic field dissolving your atomic bonds') achieves higher comment debate and shares than pure geological/exoplanet survival scenarios.
